s1.syndrome_frame: Abdominal mass with hypertension and dizziness
salient_findings: Hypoechoic lesion with clear boundary on abdominal ultrasound
Smoothly marginated soft-tissue mass on contrast-enhanced abdominal CT
Submucosal elevation on gastric fundus on upper endoscopy
key_facts: 64-year-old woman with 20-year history of hypertension
Presenting with dizziness and head discomfort for 3 days
Blood pressure at presentation was 190/100 mmHg
No gastrointestinal symptoms
Abdominal ultrasound revealed 4.7 cm × 4.4 cm hypoechoic lesion
Lesion located between upper pole of spleen and abdominal aorta
Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT showed 5.5 cm × 4.3 cm smoothly marginated soft-tissue mass
Surrounding lymph-node enlargement on CT
Upper endoscopy revealed smooth, hemispherical submucosal elevation on gastric fundus
Endoscopic ultrasonography demonstrated 3.7 cm × 4.4 cm hypoechoic, heterogeneous mass
EUS-guided fine-needle aspiration obtained scant gastric mucosal tissue and few spindle cells
Vital signs were within normal limits after blood-pressure control
Physical examination was unremarkable
Routine blood tests, blood biochemistry, fecal occult blood, and tumor markers were all normal

salient_findings: Hypoechoic lesion with clear boundary on abdominal ultrasound
Smoothly marginated soft-tissue mass on contrast-enhanced abdominal CT
Submucosal elevation on gastric fundus on upper endoscopy

Surrounding lymph-node enlargement on CT
Upper endoscopy revealed smooth, hemispherical submucosal elevation on gastric fundus

differentials: Gastric solitary fibrous tumor with malignant potential
per_call: Gastric solitary fibrous tumor with malignant potential

shortlist.label: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Incidentally revealed hypoechoic lesion with clear boundary, suggested by radiologist to originate from the stomach, and contrast-enhanced abdominal CT showed smoothly marginated soft-tissue mass with marked enhancement

shortlist.label: Leiomyoma
shortlist.why_kept: Upper endoscopy revealed smooth, hemispherical submucosal elevation on gastric fundus, and endoscopic ultrasonography demonstrated hypoechoic, heterogeneous mass arising from the muscularis propria

shortlist.label: Leiomyosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Similar presentation to leiomyoma, but with potential for malignancy, and EUS-guided fine-needle aspiration obtained scant gastric mucosal tissue and few spindle cells

shortlist.label: Gastric adenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Although no gastrointestinal symptoms, abdominal mass and lymph-node enlargement on CT raise concern for malignancy

shortlist.label: Gastric carcinoid tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Submucosal elevation on gastric fundus and hypoechoic mass on endoscopic ultrasonography could be consistent with a neuroendocrine tumor

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with a hypoechoic, heterogeneous mass arising from the muscularis propria, as demonstrated by endoscopic ultrasonography, and the presence of spindle cells on EUS-guided fine-needle aspiration, are consistent with a gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST). The location and characteristics of the mass, as well as the absence of gastrointestinal symptoms, also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Leiomyoma
rejected.why: Leiomyomas are typically smaller and less likely to cause significant lymph-node enlargement.

rejected.label: Leiomyosarcoma
rejected.why: Leiomyosarcomas are rare and usually present with more aggressive features, such as larger size, irregular margins, and higher mitotic rates, which are not described in this case.

rejected.label: Gastric adenocarcinoma
rejected.why: Gastric adenocarcinoma typically presents with mucosal ulceration, bleeding, or other gastrointestinal symptoms, which are absent in this patient.

rejected.label: Gastric carcinoid tumor
rejected.why: Gastric carcinoid tumors are usually smaller, more superficial, and have different histological features than the mass described in this case.
